QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_18

question.text: A SAS-200 drinking-water programme under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) co-funding needs the SIA to handle dual attribution. The MOST appropriate indicator for the NPO-specific contribution is:

answer.text: Number of Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) in the village — pure JJM indicator
Total households in the village including those never served
Incremental households with safe drinking water attributable to the NPO's overhead-tank / filtration-plant work, net of FHTC coverage

explanation.text: The Logic: When JJM co-funds, the SIA must isolate the incremental households served by the NPO's work over and above JJM's FHTC coverage. Pure FHTC numbers conflate both sources. The Trap: Option A double-counts JJM. Option B is denominator, not an attribution indicator. Option D is a benchmark, not attribution. Cross-Exam Context: JJM / FHTC cross-reference appears in XXIV (AML — government-scheme KYC) and the CSR-scheme overlap treated in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always pull the JJM dashboard (jaljeevanmission.gov.in) for the beneficiary villages BEFORE the field visit — it pre-identifies the overlap households and sharpens your attribution question.
